chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man was affluent, and an illness or a matter in which Allah (Exalted and Majestic) excuses him stood between him and the Hajj, then upon him is that a Sarurah (a poor person who has not performed Hajj) with no wealth for him should perform Hajj on his behalf.

key_terms.صَرُورَة: A poor person who has not performed Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an affluent person who cannot perform Hajj due to illness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *Hajj al-Badal* (substitute Hajj), where an affluent individual unable to travel due to valid excuses like illness must appoint a poor person who has not yet performed Hajj. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the financial capacity of the obligor and the spiritual eligibility of the proxy, ensuring the duty is discharged through a representative who is themselves free of the obligation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If a man was of an affluent state, and there was an illness between him and the Hajj, or a matter in which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Excused him, so upon him would be that a Saroura man (who has not performed Hajj) with no wealth for him, should perform Hajj on his behalf’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If a man is affluent but an illness or some other good reason in the sight of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, prevents him he is required (to hire) a man who has not performed any al-Hajj on his expenses to go to perform al-Hajj on his behalf.’”
